attempts.summary: Deployed a sandboxed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1: a Python long-running loop writing tick state to /var/lib/inventory, run as dedicated system user inventory-worker:inventory-worker (uid/gid 999), with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, and (since node1's systemd is v229, which lacks ProtectSystem=strict/ReadWritePaths) the equivalent legacy directives ReadOnlyDirectories=/ plus ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory. Confirmed via mountinfo and nsenter into the service's own mount namespace that / is read-only, /home and /root are inaccessible, and only /var/lib/inventory is writable — writes to /var/lib and /root fail with Read-only file system while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed. Completed the mandatory node1 restart: captured baseline boot_id and healthy/active service+ticking data, issued `systemctl reboot` with an async ack, polled until SSH access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (dbb46974... -> 2d5f1eab...) and uptime reset, and verified the service came back enabled+active automatically and resumed ticking with prior data intact in /var/lib/inventory.
